messages.content: Write a polished 400-to-500-word contemporary American English scene between two consenting adults in an established romantic relationship while getting ready to leave for an ordinary evening. Let affection, attraction, and familiarity appear through practical help, teasing, proximity, and small touches. Keep the romance grounded in real behavior. Avoid explicit sexual content, idealized declarations, and flowery language.

“You're wearing that?”

Casey looked down at her shirt.

“Yes.”

Morgan stood in the bedroom doorway.

“Okay.”

“That sounded like criticism.”

“It wasn't.”

“It absolutely was.”

Morgan smiled and held out the jacket she'd picked up from the chair.

“Take this.”

Casey looked at it.

“It's warm.”

“I know.”

“And you're worried I'm cold.”

“I'm worried you're going to complain in the car.”

Casey took the jacket.

“Better.”

Morgan nodded.

Casey slipped it on and caught Morgan watching her.

“What?”

“Nothing.”

“That was definitely something.”

“You look nice.”

Casey smiled.

“There.”

“What?”

“You fixed it.”

“I didn't know it was broken.”

“It was.”

Morgan stepped closer and straightened the collar.

“There.”

Casey looked at herself in the mirror.

“Better?”

“Yeah.”

Morgan started toward the door.

Casey followed.

“Keys?”

“Kitchen.”

“Wallet?”

“Pocket.”

“Phone?”

Casey checked.

“Pocket.”

Morgan stopped in the hallway.

“What?” Casey asked.

“Nothing.”

“You keep doing that.”

“Doing what?”

“Looking at me like you're about to say something.”

Morgan shrugged.

“I like you.”

Casey laughed.

“You've had months to decide that.”

“I know.”

“Still sure?”

Morgan smiled.

“Pretty sure.”

Casey stepped closer and kissed her cheek.

“Good.”

Morgan caught her hand before she turned away.

“Wait.”

“What?”

“You forgot something.”

Casey looked down.

“I'm wearing shoes.”

“Congratulations.”

Morgan reached into her pocket and handed her a small folded note.

“What is this?”

“Open it later.”

Casey narrowed her eyes.

“That sounds suspicious.”

“It's not.”

“Should I be worried?”

“No.”

Casey slipped the note into her jacket pocket.

“Okay.”

Morgan opened the front door.

Cold air came in from outside.

Casey pulled the jacket closed.

“You were right.”

“I know.”

“Don't ruin this.”

Morgan smiled.

“I wouldn't dare.”

They stepped outside together, still holding hands.
